senses.def: a group of three people or things
examples: A trio of teenagers was arrested for spray-painting the school.
The menu offers a trio of desserts to share.

senses.def: a group of three musicians, or a piece of music for three players
examples: A jazz trio played in the hotel lobby every evening.

note: Plural: trios.

senses.def: a journey to a place and back again, especially a short one
examples: We're taking a road trip to the Grand Canyon this summer.
He's away on a business trip until Thursday.

senses.def: to catch your foot on something and fall or almost fall
examples: I tripped over the dog's toy and nearly fell down the stairs.
Be careful not to trip on the cables.

note: "Trip" is a single journey (countable); "travel" is the general activity (uncountable). "Field trip" = school excursion.

senses.def: a great success, achievement, or victory
examples: The film was a triumph at the box office.
The landing on the moon was a triumph of science and engineering.

senses.def: the feeling of great happiness that comes from a success
examples: She raised her arms in triumph as she crossed the finish line.

note: Also a verb: "triumph over" = defeat or overcome: "Good triumphs over evil."

senses.def: (plural) soldiers, especially in large groups
examples: The government is sending more troops to the border.
US troops withdrew from the region last year.

senses.def: a group of people or animals, such as scouts or monkeys
examples: A troop of monkeys raided the campsite for food.

note: Usually plural for soldiers: "5,000 troops" = 5,000 soldiers. Don't confuse with "troupe" (a group of performers).

senses.def: an object such as a silver cup given as a prize for winning a competition
examples: The captain lifted the trophy above his head as the crowd cheered.
Her shelves are full of tennis trophies.

senses.def: something kept to show you were successful, such as part of an animal you hunted
examples: A deer's head hung on the wall as a hunting trophy.

senses.def: coming from, found in, or typical of the hot regions near the equator
examples: The hotel garden was full of tropical plants and flowers.
A tropical storm is expected to hit Florida tomorrow.

senses.def: a problem, worry, or difficulty, or a situation causing this
examples: I'm having trouble with my new phone.
The trouble is, nobody wants to pay for it.

senses.def: a situation in which you might be punished or blamed
examples: You'll be in big trouble if Mom finds out.
He was always getting into trouble at school.

senses.def: to make someone worried or upset
examples: What's troubling you? You seem quiet today.
Sorry to trouble you, but could you move your car?

note: Pattern: "have trouble + -ing": "I have trouble sleeping" (not "to sleep").

senses.def: worried and anxious
examples: She looked troubled when she read the letter.
He was deeply troubled by what he saw in the war zone.

senses.def: having a lot of problems
examples: The troubled airline has asked the government for help.
He had a troubled childhood.

note: "Troubled" = having problems; "troubling" = causing worry: "troubling news".

senses.def: (British) a piece of clothing covering the body from the waist to the ankles, with separate legs
examples: He wore a white shirt and dark trousers to the interview.
These trousers are too long; I need to get them shortened.

note: British. Americans say "pants" (in British English, "pants" means underwear). Always plural: "a pair of trousers".

senses.def: a large vehicle for carrying heavy loads by road
examples: A delivery truck was blocking the street.
He drives a truck across the country for a living.

senses.def: (American) a pickup or other small open vehicle for carrying things
examples: We loaded the furniture into the back of his truck.

note: American "truck" = British "lorry" (for large ones).

senses.def: based on facts and not invented or false
examples: Is it true that you're moving to Seattle?
The movie is based on a true story.

senses.def: real or genuine, having all the qualities of something
examples: She's a true friend; she's always there when I need her.
Their dream finally came true.

senses.def: loyal to someone or something
examples: He stayed true to his principles throughout his career.

note: "Come true" = become reality (gerçekleşmek). "Hold true" = remain valid.

senses.def: used to emphasize that something is sincere or real
examples: I'm truly sorry for what happened.
It was a truly amazing experience.

senses.def: in a real or accurate way
examples: Few people truly understand how the system works.

note: Spelled without an e: truly (not "truely"). "Yours truly" (humorous) = me.

senses.def: the belief that someone or something is honest, good, or reliable
examples: It takes years to build trust and seconds to break it.
Public trust in the media has fallen sharply.

senses.def: to believe that someone is honest and will not harm or deceive you
examples: I trust her completely.
Don't trust everything you read online.

senses.def: an arrangement in which money or property is managed by someone for another person
examples: Her grandfather left her money in a trust until she turns 25.

note: Verb takes a direct object: "I trust you" (not "trust to you"). "Trust in" is formal or religious.

senses.def: a person or organization that controls money or property kept in a trust for someone else
examples: The bank acts as trustee of the children's inheritance until they turn 21.

senses.tr: mütevelli heyeti üyesi, yönetim kurulu üyesi
senses.def: a member of a group that manages a college, charity, or similar organization
examples: The university's board of trustees approved a tuition increase.

senses.def: the true facts about something
examples: Just tell me the truth: did you break the window?
The truth is, I never wanted to move here.

senses.def: the quality of being true
examples: There is some truth in what he says.

note: Say "tell the truth" (not "say the truth").

senses.def: to make an effort to do or get something
examples: I tried to call you, but your phone was off.
Try not to be late tomorrow.

senses.def: to use or test something to see if it is good or works
examples: Have you tried the new Thai restaurant?
Try turning it off and on again.

senses.def: to examine and judge someone in a court of law
examples: He will be tried for fraud next month.

senses.def: an attempt to do something
examples: I couldn't open the jar, so I gave it another try.
It's worth a try.

note: "Try to do" = make an effort; "try doing" = experiment to see the result. "Try on" clothes = giysiyi denemek.

senses.def: an extremely large and destructive wave caused by an earthquake under the sea
examples: The earthquake triggered a tsunami that destroyed coastal villages.
Residents were warned to move to higher ground in case of a tsunami.

senses.def: a sudden, very large amount of something
examples: The company was hit by a tsunami of complaints after the update.

note: In American speech the t is often silent: /suːˈnɑːmi/.

senses.def: a long, hollow pipe through which liquids or gases can move
examples: The patient was fed through a tube for several days.
A rubber tube connects the tank to the pump.

senses.def: a soft container with a cap, used for paste or cream
examples: Squeeze the tube of toothpaste from the bottom.

senses.def: (British) the London subway; (American, informal) the television
examples: There's nothing good on the tube tonight.

note: "The Tube" is London's subway system; Americans say "the subway" for similar systems.

senses.def: the day of the week after Monday and before Wednesday
examples: The meeting has been moved to Tuesday afternoon.
Election Day in the US is always on a Tuesday.

note: Always capitalized. American pronunciation /ˈtuːz-/; British often /ˈtjuːz-/.

senses.def: (American) the money you pay to study at a college or private school
examples: College tuition has more than doubled in twenty years.
She works two jobs to pay her tuition.

senses.def: teaching, especially to one person or a small group
examples: The center offers private tuition in math and science.

note: In the US, "tuition" usually means the fee itself; in Britain it often means teaching. Americans say "tutoring" for private lessons.

senses.def: a series of musical notes that form a piece of music
examples: She was humming a tune while she cooked.
I can't get that tune out of my head.

senses.def: the state of singing or playing the correct notes
examples: The old piano is out of tune.
He can't sing in tune.

senses.def: to adjust a musical instrument or a radio or TV to the right note or station
examples: Tune in next week for the final episode.

note: "In tune with" = understanding and agreeing with: "in tune with voters". "Change your tune" = change your opinion.

senses.def: a passage built under the ground, for example for a road or railroad
examples: The train went through a long tunnel under the mountain.
The prisoners escaped through a tunnel they had dug.

collocations: light at the end of the tunnel
note: "Light at the end of the tunnel" = sign that a difficult period is ending. "Tunnel vision" = focusing on one thing only.

senses.def: to move around a central point, or to change direction
examples: Turn left at the next traffic light.
She turned the key, but the car wouldn't start.

senses.def: to change into a different state, or to reach a particular age
examples: The leaves turn red in the fall.
My son turns ten next week.

senses.def: the time when it is someone's right or duty to do something
examples: Whose turn is it to do the dishes?
Please wait your turn.

senses.def: a change of direction, or a place where a road bends
examples: Take the second turn on the right.

note: Many phrasal verbs: turn on/off (aç/kapat), turn up/down (ses aç/kıs; reddet), turn out (ortaya çıkmak).

senses.def: the number of people who come to an event or who vote in an election
examples: Voter turnout was the highest in sixty years.
Despite the rain, there was a good turnout for the charity run.

senses.def: the total value of goods or services a company sells in a period
examples: The company has an annual turnover of $50 million.

senses.tr: personel devir hızı, işten ayrılma oranı
senses.def: the rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced
examples: High staff turnover is a big problem in the restaurant industry.
Better pay helped reduce employee turnover.

note: "Turnover" for revenue is more British; Americans usually say "revenue" or "sales". "Employee turnover" is common in both.

senses.def: television, or a television set
examples: What's on TV tonight?
We bought a new TV for the living room.

note: Use "on TV" for programs: "I saw it on TV" (not "in TV").

senses.def: the number 12
examples: The flight leaves at twelve noon.
A dozen means twelve.

note: "Twelfth" is spelled with an f: twelve → twelfth.

senses.def: the number 20
examples: The store is about twenty minutes from here.
She was in her twenties when she moved to New York.

note: Americans often drop the second t in speech: /ˈtweni/. "The Roaring Twenties" = the 1920s.

senses.def: two times; on two occasions
examples: I've been to Paris twice.
Take the medicine twice a day with food.

senses.def: double in amount, size, or degree
examples: Their house is twice as big as ours.
He earns twice what I do.

note: "Think twice" = consider carefully before doing something (iki kere düşünmek).

senses.def: one of two children born to the same mother at the same time
examples: My sister and I are twins, but we don't look alike.
She gave birth to twins last spring.

senses.def: used to describe one of a pair of twins, or two similar things that form a pair
examples: His twin brother lives in Canada.
The hotel room has twin beds.

note: "Identical twins" = tek yumurta ikizleri; "fraternal twins" = çift yumurta ikizleri.

senses.def: to turn or bend something into a particular shape, or to turn something with your hand
examples: Twist the cap to open the bottle.
She twisted her hair into a bun.

senses.def: to injure a joint by turning it suddenly
examples: He twisted his ankle playing basketball.

senses.def: to change the meaning of words or facts unfairly
examples: The reporter twisted my words to make me look bad.

senses.def: an unexpected change in a story or situation, or a twisting movement
examples: The movie has a great twist at the end.
In a strange twist of fate, they met again years later.

note: "Twist someone's arm" (informal) = persuade someone: "OK, you've twisted my arm."

senses.def: the number 2
examples: We have two cats and a dog.
The movie lasts two hours.

note: Same sound as "to" and "too". "Put two and two together" = work something out from what you know.

senses.def: a group of people or things that share particular qualities; a kind or sort
examples: What type of music do you like?
There are three types of rock: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic.

senses.def: a person with a particular character, or the kind of person you are attracted to
examples: He's not really my type.
She's the outdoor type who loves camping.

senses.def: to write something using a keyboard
examples: Type your password and press Enter.
She types faster than anyone in the office.

note: "This type of car" (singular) or "these types of cars" (plural).

senses.def: having the usual qualities or features of a particular type of person, thing, or group
examples: On a typical day, I get up at six and start work at eight.
This is a typical example of colonial architecture.

senses.def: behaving in the usual way, especially in an annoying way
examples: It's typical of him to arrive late and leave early.
The bus is late again. Typical!

note: "Typical of" (not "typical for" in this sense): "That's typical of her."

senses.def: used to say that something usually happens in a particular way
examples: The trip typically takes about four hours.
Symptoms typically appear two to three days after infection.

senses.def: in a way that shows the usual qualities of a person or thing
examples: The breakfast was typically American: pancakes, eggs, and bacon.

senses.def: unpleasant to look at
examples: They tore down the ugly concrete building and built a park.
That's the ugliest sweater I've ever seen.

senses.def: (of a situation) unpleasant, violent, or threatening
examples: The argument turned ugly when someone threw a bottle.

note: Very direct about people; "unattractive" or "plain" is more polite. "Ugly duckling" = çirkin ördek yavrusu.

senses.def: happening at the end of a long process
examples: Our ultimate goal is to make the city carbon-neutral.
The ultimate decision rests with the board.

senses.tr: en büyük, en üst düzey, mükemmel
senses.def: the best, worst, or most extreme of its kind
examples: This is the ultimate guide to traveling in Japan.
Giving his life for others was the ultimate sacrifice.

note: False friend warning: "ultimate" does not mean "en son, en yeni" (latest); for that use "latest".

senses.def: in the end, after a long process
examples: The project ultimately cost twice as much as planned.
Ultimately, she decided to stay in her hometown.

senses.def: used to give the most important point
examples: Ultimately, it's your decision, not mine.

senses.def: a folding frame covered with cloth that you hold over your head to protect you from rain or sun
examples: Take an umbrella; it's supposed to rain this afternoon.
We sat under a beach umbrella all afternoon.

senses.def: something that includes or protects many different things or groups
examples: The charity works under the umbrella of the United Nations.
"Arts" is an umbrella term for music, painting, theater, and more.

note: "Umbrella organization" = çatı kuruluşu.

senses.def: not able to do something because of a lack of skill, time, strength, etc.
examples: I'm sorry, but I'm unable to attend the meeting on Friday.
Many families are unable to afford basic health care.

note: More formal than "can't". Always followed by "to + verb". The noun is "inability", not "unability".

senses.def: so bad or wrong that it should not be allowed
examples: Racist comments are completely unacceptable in this workplace.
Waiting six hours in the emergency room is unacceptable.

senses.def: the state of not being sure, or something that is not known or decided
examples: Economic uncertainty is making companies cautious about hiring.
There is still some uncertainty about the cause of the crash.

senses.def: the brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt
examples: My uncle taught me how to fish.
We're spending Christmas with my aunt and uncle in Denver.

note: One English word for amca, dayı, and enişte. Specify if needed: "my mom's brother".

senses.def: not physically comfortable, or unpleasant to wear, sit on, etc.
examples: These shoes are really uncomfortable.
We spent the night on uncomfortable plastic chairs.

senses.def: feeling embarrassed, nervous, or anxious
examples: I felt uncomfortable when they started arguing in front of me.
There was an uncomfortable silence after his joke.

note: Pronounced with three or four syllables: /ʌnˈkʌmftəbl/; the "or" is usually silent.

senses.def: in a state like sleep, because of an injury or illness, and unable to see, feel, or think
examples: He was knocked unconscious in the crash.
She was found unconscious on the kitchen floor.

senses.def: happening without you being aware of it
examples: Many hiring decisions are influenced by unconscious bias.

note: Medical sense = baygın. "Unconscious" does not mean "careless" (bilinçsizce davranan → thoughtless, careless).

senses.def: in or to a position below or covered by something
examples: The cat is hiding under the bed.
We sat under a tree to get out of the sun.

senses.def: less than a particular amount, age, or level
examples: Children under 12 get in free.
You can get a good laptop for under $500.

senses.def: controlled by someone, or affected by a process or situation
examples: The bridge is under construction.
She's been under a lot of pressure lately.

senses.def: below the surface of water, or less than a certain amount
examples: The boat went under in the storm.
Kids aged ten and under eat free.

note: "Under way" = already started. "Under the circumstances" = bu şartlar altında.

senses.def: to experience something, especially a change or something unpleasant
examples: She underwent surgery on her knee last week.
The city has undergone major changes in the last decade.

note: Irregular: undergo – underwent – undergone. Formal; common with medical procedures and changes.

senses.def: a university or college student studying for a first degree
examples: The course is open to undergraduates in their final year.
As an undergraduate, he worked part-time in the library.

note: Often used as an adjective: "undergraduate degree" = lisans derecesi. Informal: "undergrad".

senses.def: under the surface of the ground
examples: The building has an underground parking garage.
Miners were trapped in an underground tunnel.

senses.def: under the surface of the ground
examples: The cables run underground along the highway.

senses.def: secret and often illegal, or not part of the mainstream culture
examples: During the war, she worked for an underground resistance group.
The band started out in the underground music scene.

note: "The Underground" is the London subway; Americans say "the subway". "Go underground" = hide from authorities.

senses.def: to be the real basis or cause of something, often not easily noticed
examples: Poverty and lack of education underlie many of the city's problems.
The same basic principle underlies all of these designs.

note: Formal. Irregular like "lie": underlie – underlay – underlain. Most often seen as the adjective "underlying".
